verdict.headline: Cisco's beat-and-raise sell extends to 6% pre-market; July PPI at 8:30 decides the 30-year path
verdict.label: CSCO AH sell extends overnight to −6% (~$116); PPI (8:30 AM) is the 30Y pivot; AMAT after close is the semi-equipment follow-on
verdict.rationale_short: CSCO's initial 4% after-hours sell on a genuine beat-and-raise has widened to ~6% pre-market (−$7.92 to ~$116 from $123.88), firming the 'good news already priced' ceiling for AI infrastructure entering NVDA's August 26 print. July PPI (8:30 AM ET) is the session's binary: energy is expected to deflate 3%, but WTI held $82–83 through July's measurement window, embedding costs the CPI core did not surface. A hot energy line sends September odds back above 40% and re-anchors the 30Y above 5.25%; in-line or soft PPI confirms the first 30Y compression path toward 5.15% before Jackson Hole. Level that changes the morning read: 30Y closes below 5.20% on in-line-or-soft PPI AND September odds hold below 38%.

watchlist_mentions.note: Pre-market ~$220.88 (−1.1% from $223.40 close). The CSCO template is the new framework: a genuine beat-and-raise at altitude sold off 6% — meeting the gross margin above 76% and guide above consensus bar on August 26 may not be sufficient to expand the multiple. $225 first resistance; $216 structural support. Jackson Hole on August 27 arrives one day after the print.

Pre-market ~$116 (−6% from $123.88 regular close; initial AH was −4%). The session's defining overnight signal: AI infrastructure names at altitude have a pricing ceiling. Revenue $17.3B (beat), EPS $1.22 (beat), $9.3B FY26 AI orders, FY27 guidance $72.2-73.4B above consensus — none of it was enough. The reaction, not the result, is the signal.

~$539 pre-market, reporting Q3 FY2026 after close today. Consensus: $3.36 EPS / $9.0B revenue (+35.5% YoY). At $539, AMAT is 27% below its year-to-date peak of $739. A beat and strong forward guidance tests whether CSCO's sell-off is stock-specific (networking already priced) or ecosystem-wide (semi-equipment demand softening). AMAT AH above $550 on a beat = CSCO template contained; AMAT AH below $520 on a miss = template broadens.

$107.96 (Aug 12 close). No direct overnight catalyst. CSCO's extended pre-market sell is the first like-instance data point at altitude: a strong AI infrastructure beat-and-raise drew sellers, not buyers. Net loss expanded $626M from $290M YoY; the $104B backlog and capex-to-revenue structure are unchanged. Next inflection: the level where the thesis changes is backlog below $95B in a subsequent quarter.

~$499 (Aug 12 close). Yesterday's $484 floor resolution (+3.02%) stands. PPI is the next rate-environment test; a hot print re-anchors September odds above 40% and applies renewed multiple pressure. $484 remains the key support level.
~$174.94 (Aug 12 close). Iran's ongoing Hormuz attacks and escalation structurally support DoD AI spend — the thesis carried since Q2. No new direct catalyst today.
$302.25 (Aug 12 close). Continued underperformance in an otherwise green session Wednesday. Jefferies Underperform (PT $263.66) remains the only recent analyst signal. No catalyst today.

~$139.05 (Aug 12 close). August 20 tranche (~7%, ~$8.65B eligible) is 7 days away. Oil regime conditions partially eased: WTI fell to $81.41 (above $79 trigger but closer to it), Brent to $87.17 (above $85 trigger). Trump Hormuz rhetoric drove the oil decline; the structural gap between rhetoric and Iran's blockade condition means the regime hasn't cleared. Front-run signal: close below $120 on elevated volume before August 20.

~$63,402 (Aug 12 close). Gate 2 ($62K) buffer narrowed to ~$1.4K from $2.2K at the prior brief's first read. September odds at ~40% provide modest hike-risk reduction; PPI today is the next macro input. Below $62K triggers the next regime gate.

trade_setups.asset: 30Y Yield — PPI energy component and the path to 5.15%
trade_setups.thesis: The 30Y at 5.236% is on its 14th consecutive session above the 5.00% trigger. It held flat on a below-expected CPI core (2.5%), suggesting the bond market's prior requires more than one month's data. PPI's energy component — where WTI's $82-83 July average embeds costs the CPI service-side core did not capture — is the next test. Below 5.20% post-PPI would be the first concrete de-escalation signal; above 5.28% re-establishes the rate overhang entering Jackson Hole.
trade_setups.entry: 30Y at 5.236%. Watch post-8:30 AM reaction: below 5.20% = first de-escalation signal; above 5.28% = regime re-entrenches. The 5.00% trigger is the formal threshold; 5.15% is the compression target the prior brief identified.
trade_setups.invalidation: 30Y closes below 5.10% on two consecutive sessions — the trigger formally clearing.
trade_setups.horizon: Today's PPI print through Jackson Hole keynote August 27.

trade_setups.asset: AMAT — the CSCO counter-test for semi-equipment demand
trade_setups.thesis: CSCO's beat-and-raise sold because AI networking infrastructure orders were priced in, not because demand is declining. AMAT (after close) is the capital equipment layer — the picks-and-shovels for the chips that power the AI stack. If AMAT beats on forward guidance and semiconductor equipment demand holds, CSCO's sell is stock-specific. If AMAT's guidance disappoints alongside CSCO, the altitude ceiling extends to the broader semi-equipment complex and sharpens the NVDA August 26 setup risk.
trade_setups.entry: AMAT ~$539 ahead of the print; 27% below the year-to-date peak of $739. AH above $550 on a beat = CSCO template is contained in networking; AH below $520 on a miss = template broadens into equipment.
trade_setups.invalidation: AMAT beats on all metrics and raises forward semiconductor capex demand above prior guidance.
trade_setups.horizon: AMAT after-close today through NVDA August 26.

trade_setups.asset: SPCX — August 20 tranche as oil moves toward the trigger
trade_setups.thesis: WTI fell 2.2% overnight to $81.41 on Trump Hormuz rhetoric — still above the $79 trigger but narrowing the buffer. Brent at $87.17 (above $85). The oil-side headwind is partially easing via rhetoric, not structural deal progress; Iran's condition (lift the naval blockade) is unchanged. If WTI closes below $79 on two consecutive sessions before August 20, one of the two active oil-side triggers clears ahead of the supply gate, changing the absorption thesis.
trade_setups.entry: SPCX ~$139.05. August 20 is the gate (~$8.65B eligible). WTI $81.41 (above $79 trigger); two consecutive closes below $79 clears the oil-side condition. Front-run signal: SPCX close below $120 on elevated volume before August 20.
trade_setups.invalidation: WTI closes below $79 on two consecutive sessions, removing the primary oil trigger.
trade_setups.horizon: Through August 20 tranche and October Q3 earnings.

bear_case: The 30Y's failure to compress on a below-threshold CPI core (2.5%) is not noise — it is the bond market's explicit statement that one month's service-side data does not offset its inflation prior, and PPI's energy component carries the oil-price cost that CPI missed. CSCO's beat-and-raise selling off 6% overnight establishes that the AI infrastructure multiple is not expanding from current levels regardless of the result quality. NVDA at $223.40 enters August 26 with no comparable situation where a genuine beat-and-raise expanded the multiple at altitude. If PPI energy surprises above −1% (less deflationary than forecast) and September odds climb to 45%, the scenario where the 30Y re-anchors at 5.28% entering the NVDA print becomes the base case, not the tail. Level that invalidates the equity-resilience read: 30Y holds above 5.28% after the PPI print AND SPX closes below 7,600 within two sessions.
